about: ENOVATE Motors is described by Crunchbase as an automotive industry company based in Shanghai, China, with the input listing automotive, energy and mobility among its industries. Funding shown is about CNY 7.75bn with the latest round in March 2023. The input gives no more detail on its vehicles, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Ford Otosan is a Turkish vehicle manufacturer based in Kocaeli, a joint venture between Ford Motor Company and the Koc Group, each holding about 41 percent. It makes the Transit and Puma family, Courier and heavy trucks including the F-MAX, at plants in Golcuk, Yeniköy and Craiova (Romania), plus a growing EV business. It exports across Europe. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (FROTO). Leading brand in Turkey's commercial vehicle market, with F1 and Ford-linked marketing exposure.

ROX Motor is described by Crunchbase as a Shanghai-based car-making project focusing on off-road electric vehicles, with industries listed as automotive and electric vehicles. Funding shown is about $1.38bn with the latest round in September 2023. The input gives no more detail on models, sales or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Zeekr is the premium electric vehicle brand of Geely Holding, based in Hangzhou, making models such as the Zeekr 001, 007, 009 MPV and X. It sells in China, Europe and other markets and listed on the NYSE (ZK) in 2024, then was taken private by Geely Automobile in a 2025 merger. Vehicle deliveries exceeded 200,000 a year. Strong Chinese premium EV brand, building awareness in Europe, with sponsorship activity in sport and F1-adjacent events.

Arrival was a London-based electric vehicle maker, founded in 2015, which designed electric vans and buses built in micro-factories, with backing from Hyundai, Kia and UPS, and listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC in 2021. It ran out of money, and its UK arm entered administration in early 2024. Funding was about $1.0bn. Now defunct as a manufacturer, with no active commercial relevance.

Hyundai Mobis is a Seoul-based South Korean auto parts maker, the largest supplier to Hyundai Motor Group, producing modules (chassis, cockpit, front-end), electrification parts, ADAS sensors, lamps and aftermarket parts, with global sales near KRW 60 trillion. It also runs a Mobis parts aftersales business. Listed on the Korea Exchange (012330), with Hyundai-affiliated groups as major shareholders. Mostly B2B, known to the auto industry, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Blue Bird Corporation is a Macon, Georgia manufacturer of school buses, including Type A, C and D buses, plus electric, propane and CNG versions, with a strong share of the US and Canadian school bus market. Customers are school districts, contractors and transit agencies, and revenue is about $1.3bn. Listed on Nasdaq (BLBD). Founded in 1927. B2B and institutional manufacturer, the yellow bus is iconic but the corporate brand has low direct consumer awareness. Crunchbase country is shown as Georgia (the US state).

DST Car (Shenzhen Dongshangtong, Dingshentong) is a Chinese new energy vehicle rental and mobility platform based in Shenzhen, operating electric car and ride-hailing fleet leasing to drivers and consumers across Chinese cities. It earns lease and rental income. Funding is about $729m, with backers including Chinese investment funds. Private. Business-to-driver service with a regional consumer audience in China and no international brand.

Getaround is a Paris-founded car-sharing marketplace, now US-based after a 2022 SPAC merger, letting owners rent out vehicles to drivers through its app with keyless access, in cities in the US and Europe. It earns a share of rental fees and insurance. It was listed on the NYSE (GETR) and exited the US market in early 2025, wound down parts of its business and focuses on Europe. Funding about $763m. A consumer-facing mobility app with modest awareness.

Horse Powertrain is a London-registered powertrain company formed in 2022 as a joint venture between Renault Group and Geely, with Aramco joining as a 10 percent investor in 2024. It builds combustion engines, hybrid systems and transmissions, with plants and R&D in Europe, Brazil, China and Turkey, and about 19,000 employees. Customers include Renault, Dacia, Geely brands and other carmakers. B2B component maker, with the Horse name known in the car industry only.

JSW Motors is the automotive arm of India's JSW Group, based in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra, set up to build electric and new-energy vehicles in India, including a tie-up to market MG-branded cars through JSW MG Motor, formerly SAIC-owned MG Motor India. It plans a large new factory with investment of about INR 80bn. Part of the JSW conglomerate led by Sajjan Jindal. Early-stage brand with growing but limited consumer awareness; JSW is a notable Indian sports sponsor.

Rimac Group is a Croatian electric hypercar and technology company based near Zagreb, formed from Rimac Automobili (maker of the Nevera) and Bugatti Rimac, which owns Bugatti, and Rimac Technology, a supplier of battery systems and drivetrains for carmakers such as Porsche, Aston Martin and Koenigsegg. Founded by Mate Rimac in 2009, its investors include Porsche (about 45 percent) and Hyundai/Kia. Private. Very high profile among car enthusiasts, with its hypercar sales limited to a few hundred units.

Dongchedi (Car Home competitor) is the Chinese automotive information and car-buying platform from ByteDance, offering reviews, pricing, live-streams, videos and lead generation for car dealers and automakers, with a mobile app and Douyin integration. It earns advertising and lead fees from automakers and dealers. Part of ByteDance, which is privately held, with about $600m funding listed. Strong brand among Chinese car shoppers, very little outside China.

Kyte is a San Francisco company, founded in 2020, that delivers rental cars to customers' doors in US cities through a driver handover app, with a marketplace focus on convenience and subscription flexibility. It earns rental and delivery fees and has been backed by Chicago-based and other investors. Funding shown is about $549m including debt. Private. Small consumer mobility brand with limited national awareness.

Plastic Omnium (rebranded OPmobility in 2024) is a French automotive supplier based in Levallois-Perret, making exterior body parts, bumpers, fuel and hydrogen storage systems, lighting, and e-mobility systems for car makers worldwide, with revenue near EUR 11bn and about 40,000 employees. Controlled by Burelle SA and the Burelle family. Listed on Euronext Paris (OPM). B2B supplier, with brand known to the auto industry rather than consumers.

Spiro (Spironet) is a Nairobi-linked, Africa-focused electric motorcycle and battery-swap company, founded in Benin and growing in Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Togo and Nigeria, selling electric motorcycles and swap networks to boda-boda taxi riders and delivery fleets. Funding is about $575m according to Crunchbase. Private, backed by Afreximbank, Equator and others. Growing brand among African commercial riders, with little international consumer awareness.

Allison Transmission Holdings is an Indianapolis maker of fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles, buses, fire trucks, defence vehicles and off-highway equipment, along with electrified propulsion systems. It sells to truck and bus makers and the military, with revenue of about $3bn and plants in Indiana and Hungary and India. Listed on the NYSE (ALSN). B2B supplier; the brand is known to fleet operators but not to consumers.

AMAG Leasing is the automotive leasing and financing arm of the AMAG Group, Switzerland's largest car importer and dealer, based in Cham, Zug. It leases and finances Volkswagen, Audi, SEAT, Skoda and other vehicles to private customers and businesses in Switzerland. AMAG Group is privately owned by the Haefner family. Funding shown is CHF 450m. Local B2B2C finance brand with limited visibility outside Switzerland.

ECD Automotive Design is a Kissimmee, Florida company that restores and customises classic Land Rover Defenders and Range Rovers, and since 2024 other vehicles, as bespoke luxury builds, sometimes with electric conversions, with prices well into six figures. It builds vehicles for wealthy individual clients and shows them on social media and TV. Listed on the NYSE (ECDA) in 2023 via a SPAC merger. Niche premium brand with strong social-media following among car enthusiasts.

Global Lending Services (GLS) is a US auto finance company serving consumers with subprime or near-prime vehicle loans and leases through dealers, with offices in Greenville, South Carolina and Atlanta. It earns interest and fees on loans, funded through debt facilities of about $500m. Private. B2B2C lender known to dealers, with little consumer brand awareness. Limited public detail beyond the input.

about: Zero Motorcycles is a Scotts Valley, California maker of electric motorcycles, including the SR/F, SR/S and DS lines, sold through dealers in North America, Europe and Asia to consumers, as well as to police and fleets. Founded in 2006 by Neal Saiki, it has raised hundreds of millions from investors such as Invus and Mahindra-linked backers. Private. Known among motorcycle enthusiasts, with a modest brand presence.

Chunqing Technology is described by Crunchbase as a Chinese company creating a new generation of electric vehicles, listed as based in Tianjin, with Guangdong appearing in the location field. The input lists automotive and electric vehicle industries and funding of about $435m with the latest round in July 2025. No more detail on products, customers or owners is given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Garmin is a GPS technology company, legally Swiss and operating from Olathe, Kansas, making GPS wearables and smartwatches (Forerunner, fenix, Venu), cycling computers, marine electronics, aviation avionics, automotive navigation and in-car systems. It sells to consumers and OEM customers worldwide, with revenue near $7bn and about 20,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GRMN). Strong consumer brand among athletes, pilots and boaters, and a sports sponsor including sailing, cycling and motorsport.

Vertelo is an Indian fleet electrification and EV leasing platform based in Mumbai, backed by Mahindra Group's venture and others, offering electric vehicles on lease or financing to delivery and mobility fleets without upfront ownership cost. It earns lease income and services, and arranged about $400m including debt. Private. B2B fleet finance brand, known to logistics operators and little to consumers.

Harbinger is a Garden Grove, California electric commercial vehicle maker, founded in 2022, building medium-duty electric truck chassis for delivery fleets, school buses and utility vehicles in the US, with Ford-linked backing. It raised about $358m in total, including a 2025 round. Private. B2B fleet supplier with low public awareness.

Hella is a Lippstadt, Germany automotive supplier of lighting, electronics and aftermarket parts, a century-old brand now majority-owned by Faurecia, which took control in 2022 and combined to form Forvia. Hella makes headlights, tail lights, sensors, ADAS radar and electronics for carmakers, plus a workshop-and-parts business. Part of Forvia (Euronext: FRVIA). Respected in the automotive trade, with limited direct consumer awareness; Hella has sponsored motorsport.

Tier IV is a Tokyo autonomous driving software company, founded in 2015, which develops and maintains the open-source Autoware platform and licenses self-driving software for buses, trucks and robotaxis. Investors include Yamaha Motor, Suzuki, Sompo and Sony-affiliated funds, and it works with Japanese cities and mobility operators. Private. B2B technology known in autonomous driving circles, with no consumer awareness.

Wallbox is a Barcelona-based maker of electric vehicle chargers, including home Pulsar units, public DC fast chargers and bidirectional chargers, plus energy management software, selling to consumers, businesses and utilities in Europe, North America and Asia. Revenue is about EUR 150m and losses are heavy. Listed on the NYSE (WBX) via a 2021 SPAC merger. Known to EV owners, with moderate consumer awareness.

Battery Smart is a Gurugram, India EV battery swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, with hundreds of swap stations across Indian cities, mainly serving rickshaw and delivery drivers, who pay per swap. Founded in 2019, it raised about $285m including investments from Blume Ventures, Tiger Global, Trifecta Capital and Mahindra-linked funds. Private. Popular among commercial EV drivers, with low mainstream consumer awareness.

Euler Motors is a New Delhi-based Indian electric vehicle maker producing the HiLoad electric three-wheeler cargo vehicle and the Storm electric light truck for last-mile delivery, serving fleet customers. It is backed by Blume Ventures, Lightspeed and Bajaj Auto-linked investors, and has raised about $300m. Private. Strong in the commercial EV segment, with low consumer awareness.

Greenway is an electric vehicle charging network operator based in Bratislava, Slovakia, which runs fast and ultra-fast public chargers across Central and Eastern Europe, including Slovakia, Poland, Czechia and the Balkans. Customers are EV drivers using its app and card, and fleets. Funding is about EUR 273m including investment from Meridiam-style infrastructure investors. Private. Known to EV drivers in the region, little awareness elsewhere.

about: Motorway is a London-based online used-car selling platform, launched in 2017, where private sellers upload a car and a network of dealers bid, with the seller paying no fee. Dealers pay a fee on completed sales, and it sold over 100,000 cars a year. Backed by DST Global, Highland Europe and others, with funding of about $324m. Private. Well-advertised consumer brand in the UK.

RideNow Powersports is a Chandler, Arizona operator of motorcycle, ATV and powersports dealerships, with over 100 stores in the US selling brands such as Harley-Davidson, Honda, Yamaha, Polaris and Can-Am. It earns from vehicle sales, parts, service and financing. Owned by private equity (Lee Equity Partners and later Argonaut-style sponsors), with funding of about $255m. Private. Recognised by US riders, and active in racing and rally sponsorships.

SEDEMAC is a Pune-based Indian maker of electronic controllers and drives for engines, generators, electric vehicles and appliances, including gensets, diesel engines, e-bikes and e-scooters. It spun out of IIT Bombay research in 2008 and supplies companies such as Mahindra, Kirloskar, Cummins, Honda and Bajaj. Funding is about $260m from investors including Mahindra-linked and ADB-style capital. Private. B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Simple Energy is a Bengaluru-based Indian electric scooter maker, founded in 2019, selling the Simple One and Dot One scooters with a high range, through its own stores, and building a fast-charging network. Backed by Mathew Kuruvilla-led founders, Qualcomm Ventures-style and other investors, it has raised about $280m, including debt. Private. Growing consumer EV brand with limited national awareness.

Suzuki Motor de Mexico is the Mexican subsidiary of Japan's Suzuki Motor Corporation, based in Cuautitlan Izcalli, distributing and marketing Suzuki cars, SUVs and motorcycles in Mexico through a dealer network, and assembling some in Mexico. Funding shown is MXN 4.9bn, a capital-style figure. Subsidiary of Suzuki (Tokyo: 7269). Strong consumer brand in Mexico, with sponsorships in motorsport and local sports.

Calidda is Gas Natural de Lima y Callao, the Lima-based Peruvian company that distributes natural gas to homes, businesses, industry and vehicles in Lima and Callao, with a concession covering millions of residents. It earns regulated tariffs for gas connections and supply. Owned mostly by Grupo Energia Bogota (Colombia), with Promigas. Private. Utility brand well known in Lima, with some community sponsorship, and an automotive gas conversion business.

Moove is a Lagos, Nigeria-based mobility fintech that finances vehicles for ride-hailing and delivery drivers, offering vehicle leases, fleet management and revenue-based financing across Africa, India and the UK, working with Uber, Bolt and Lyft partners. It raised about $694m, including a $100m Series B from Uber and Mubadala in 2023. Private. Known among rideshare drivers and fleet operators, with limited public consumer awareness.

DeepWay is a Hefei, Anhui-based Chinese company developing intelligent electric heavy-duty trucks and autonomous driving systems for logistics, including electric and hydrogen trucks, as part of Baidu's former and Chinese investor-backed commercial vehicle push. It has raised about $590m, with a January 2026 round. Private, with an IPO plan in Hong Kong. B2B logistics technology brand, known in Chinese trucking, with no consumer awareness.

Kodiak Robotics is a Mountain View, California autonomous trucking company, founded in 2018 by ex-Google and Uber self-driving engineers, developing the Kodiak Driver for long-haul freight. Customers are trucking and logistics firms, with driverless operations in the Texas oil-field region for Atlas Energy and a long-haul network in the US Sun Belt. It went public via a SPAC merger with Ares Acquisition Corp II in 2025 (Nasdaq: KDK). B2B technology, limited consumer brand awareness.

about: Shouqi Car Rental is a Beijing-based Chinese car rental and ride-hailing business, associated with the state-owned Beijing Shouqi Group (formerly Capital Automobile). It operates the Shouqi Limousine and Chauffeur brand, a premium ride-hailing service for consumers and corporate clients, and extended car rental. Last funding was in 2016. Moderate brand awareness in China, B2B and mid-market consumer. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Li Auto is a Beijing-based Chinese electric vehicle maker, founded in 2015 as Chehejia and led by Li Xiang. It sells extended-range EV SUVs (L-series) and, since 2024, the battery EV Mega and i-series, alongside its own charging network. It sells through direct stores to Chinese consumers, with annual deliveries of several hundred thousand vehicles. Listed on Nasdaq (LI) and Hong Kong (2015). Strong consumer brand in China, expanding abroad.

Qingju is a bike-sharing platform based in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, listed under electric vehicle and product industries. The input describes it as a company providing bike-sharing platforms; it reports about $2 billion in funding with the last round in February 2021. It was later associated with the Didi group's shared bike business, but the input does not confirm ownership. Consumer service in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Chery Holding is a Wuhu, China-based state-linked automaker, one of China's largest carmakers and top vehicle exporters, owning the Chery, Exeed, Jetour, iCar and Omoda brands and a joint venture with JLR (Freelander in China). It sells passenger cars and SUVs, including EVs, in over 100 countries. Its subsidiary Chery Automobile listed in Hong Kong in 2025 (9973). Consumer car brand with growing recognition in Europe, Latin America and emerging markets, and a football and sports sponsor.

Bird (Bird Global) is a Miami-based micro-mobility company that operated e-scooter and e-bike sharing across US and European cities. Founded in 2017 by Travis VanderZanden, it went public via SPAC in 2021 (NYSE: BRDS), and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2023; it was bought out by its Third Lane Mobility affiliate in 2024. Consumers rent via app. Familiar urban consumer brand through its scooters, now much smaller.

Linamar is a Guelph, Ontario-based Canadian precision manufacturer of vehicle powertrain components, drivetrain systems and structural parts, plus Skyjack access platforms and agricultural equipment (MacDon). Customers are global automakers such as GM, Ford and Stellantis. Founded in 1966 by Frank Hasenfratz, it has about 32,000 employees in 17 countries and revenue near C$10 billion. Listed on the TSX (LNR). B2B supplier with little consumer awareness.

Nu Ride is the successor of Lordstown Motors, the Ohio electric vehicle maker that went bankrupt in 2023 after producing the Endurance pickup and then emerged as a shell company with litigation claims against Foxconn. The input says it is expanding into insurance. Reported funding is about $1.09 billion, historical. Listed on Nasdaq (RIDE). Small shell, no active consumer products. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Sokon is a Chinese automotive manufacturer (Chongqing Sokon Industry Group, brand Seres, associated with the Seres-Huawei Aito partnership) that develops and manufactures automobiles, new energy vehicles and engines. Seres Group is listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong. The input lists funding of about 7.1 billion yuan. Consumer-facing through Aito vehicles in China, but little brand awareness abroad.

about: Tata Passenger Electric Mobility (TPEML) is the electric vehicle subsidiary of Tata Motors in India, selling the Tata Nexon EV, Tiago EV, Punch EV and Curvv EV and running charging infrastructure, with leading share of the Indian passenger EV market. TPG Rise Climate invested about 75 billion rupees in 2021. Customers are Indian consumers and fleets. Tata Motors passenger vehicles are listed as Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles after a 2025 demerger. High consumer brand awareness in India.

McLaren Group is a Woking, England-based automotive, motorsport and technology group, comprising McLaren Automotive (supercars and hypercars), McLaren Racing (Formula 1, IndyCar, Formula E, Extreme E), McLaren Applied and McLaren Technology Centre. Founded by Bruce McLaren in 1963. Controlled by Bahrain's Mumtalakat sovereign fund with additional minority investors. Automotive was sold to CYVN Holdings in 2025. Very strong consumer brand and an established F1 team with large sponsorship programme.

ABB is a Zurich-based Swiss-Swedish multinational technology group in electrification, automation, motion and robotics, serving utilities, industry, transport and buildings in about 100 countries. Revenue is roughly $33 billion, with about 110,000 employees. It also runs the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship title sponsorship and EV charging (Terra chargers). Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and Nasdaq Stockholm (ABBN). B2B, high business awareness and a notable sports sponsor.

Canoo was a Torrance, California electric vehicle maker that developed a modular skateboard-based platform and a multi-purpose delivery van and lifestyle vehicle. Founded in 2017, it went public via SPAC in 2020 (Nasdaq: GOEV), won orders from NASA and the US Postal Service, and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in January 2025. Reported funding about $595 million. Defunct, so not a prospect. Had modest consumer awareness during its funding rounds.

CelLink is a San Carlos, California manufacturer of flexible circuits for electric vehicle batteries and other clean energy applications, offering high-conductance, large-area flexible wiring harnesses that replace traditional cables. Founded in 2013. Customers include automakers and battery makers, and the input reports funding of about $659 million. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Turo is a San Francisco peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace, founded in 2009 (as RelayRides), where owners list cars and travellers rent them via app in the US, Canada, UK, Australia and France. It earns a commission on bookings. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Shell Ventures and others, with about $590 million raised. It withdrew its IPO plans in 2022. Strong consumer awareness among US travellers and heavy digital advertising.

BluSmart Mobility is a Gurugram-based Indian all-electric ride-hailing and cab fleet operator that ran an app-based service in Delhi, Bengaluru and Mumbai using its own EV fleet and charging hubs, founded in 2019 by the Gensol group's Anmol and Puneet Jaggi. It collapsed in 2025 amid a governance scandal involving the funds diverted by its parent Gensol, and operations were suspended. Reported funding is about $486 million. Defunct. Was a recognised consumer brand in Indian metros.

Infinitum is an Austin, Texas maker of high-efficiency electric motors (the Aircore range) used in data center cooling, HVAC, industrial equipment and vehicles. The motors use a printed circuit board stator to cut weight and energy use. Customers are OEMs and industrial and data center operators. Reported funding is about $458 million. B2B industrial technology, with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Spotawheel is a Greek tech-driven used-car dealership platform that sells and buys pre-owned vehicles online with inspection, financing and warranty services, operating in Greece and Europe. Founded around 2019 in Athens, it is backed by Greek and international investors and reported funding of about 418 million euros. Consumers are used-car buyers and sellers. Regional brand awareness in Greece. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: CLIP Group is a logistics group, listed in the input as based in Nicaragua, providing warehousing and related logistics services. about: Hyzon Motors is a US maker of hydrogen fuel-cell heavy trucks and fuel-cell systems, founded in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2021 (HYZN). It struggled with sales and an SEC investigation and wound down operations and liquidated in early 2025. Reported funding about $405 million. Customers were commercial fleets in the US and Europe. Defunct, with limited brand awareness.

LeddarTech is a Quebec City-based Canadian automotive technology company, founded in 2007, offering LeddarVision sensor fusion and perception software and LeddarEngine lidar technology for ADAS and autonomous driving. Customers are automakers and Tier-1 suppliers. It listed on Nasdaq (LDTC) via SPAC in 2023 and has raised about $400 million. B2B automotive technology, with no consumer brand awareness.

REE Automotive is an Israeli electric vehicle platform company, based in Tel Aviv, designing modular drive-by-wire skateboard platforms that place the drivetrain, steering and suspension in the wheel arches for commercial vehicles. Founded in 2013 and listed on Nasdaq (REE) in 2021 via SPAC. It scaled back after problems getting vehicles to market and stopped production plans in 2025. Reported funding about $404 million. B2B, limited brand awareness.

Zunder is a Spanish electric vehicle charging company, based in the Basque Country, that builds and operates fast and ultra-fast charging networks along motorways and in cities, for EV drivers and fleets. Reported funding is about 387 million euros, mostly for infrastructure investment. Moderate brand awareness among EV drivers in Spain. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Ample is a San Francisco company, founded in 2014, that developed modular battery swapping stations for electric vehicles, using robotic stations that swap battery modules in a few minutes. It piloted with Uber drivers in San Francisco, ran fleets in Madrid and Japan with Stellantis and Mitsubishi Fuso, and filed for bankruptcy in 2025. Reported funding about $327 million. Defunct. Limited consumer awareness.

Dott is an Amsterdam-based European micro-mobility operator, founded in 2018 by Henri Moissinac, offering shared e-scooters and e-bikes via app in cities such as Paris, London, Brussels and Madrid. It merged with Tier Mobility in 2024 to form the largest shared-mobility company in Europe, with Dott as the brand. Reported funding about $328 million. Consumer-facing urban brand with high visibility on streets.

Droom is a Gurugram-based Indian online marketplace for automobiles, founded in 2014 by Sandeep Aggarwal, where users buy, sell and finance new and used cars, two-wheelers and other vehicles, with its Droom Credit and inspection services. Reported funding about $336 million. Customers are Indian consumers and dealers. Moderate consumer awareness in India.

JingXi ZhiXing is a Chinese automotive supplier of vehicle chassis suspension systems and components, such as air springs and shock absorbers, manufacturing automotive parts for car makers. The input reports funding of 2.5 billion yuan. It is based in China. B2B supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Park-Ohio Holdings is a Cleveland, Ohio industrial supply chain logistics and diversified manufacturing company, serving customers in automotive, aerospace, appliance and energy through its Supply Technologies and Assembly Components businesses. Revenue is about $1.6 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (PKOH). B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

BMW Group is a Munich-based luxury automaker founded in 1916, producing BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce cars and BMW Motorrad motorcycles. It sells around 2.5 million vehicles a year across 140 countries with revenue near 140 billion euros and about 150,000 employees. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (BMW) and controlled by the Quandt family. Customers are consumers and fleets. Global premium brand with a long history in motorsport and in F1 sponsorship and partnerships.

May Mobility is an Ann Arbor, Michigan self-driving technology company, founded in 2017, that designs and operates autonomous vehicles for shared mobility, running driverless shuttle and ride-hail services in US cities with partners including Toyota, Lyft and Uber. Raised about $310 million; it announced a SPAC merger in 2025 to list on Nasdaq. Customers are cities, transit agencies and mobility platforms. Limited consumer brand awareness.

NASN Automotive Electronics is a Chinese manufacturer of automotive electronic components, particularly tyre pressure monitoring systems (TPMS) and related sensors for car makers. It is based in China, listed on the Shenzhen exchange, and the input shows reported funding of about $294 million. B2B automotive supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

about: ArcBest is a Fort Smith, Arkansas logistics company providing less-than-truckload freight (ABF Freight), expedited and asset-light logistics solutions for shippers across North America. Founded in 1923, with about 14,000 employees and revenue of around $4.5 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (ARCB). Customers are businesses. B2B transportation brand with limited consumer awareness.

Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC Group) is a Guangzhou, China state-owned automaker, listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (601238, 2238), making vehicles under GAC Trumpchi, GAC Aion (EV) and Hyptec, and in joint ventures with Toyota, Honda and Mitsubishi. It also has financial services and parts businesses. Sells hundreds of thousands to over 2 million vehicles a year. Strong consumer brand in China and a growing export business.

Terra Motors is a Japanese electric vehicle maker, founded in 2010, producing electric two- and three-wheelers and e-rickshaws, sold mainly in India and Southeast Asia. The input lists automotive and autonomous categories and funding of about $255 million. Customers are consumers and commercial operators. Limited global brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: DeepBlue Auto (Deepal) is a Chongqing, China new energy vehicle brand of Changan Automobile, selling the Deepal-branded SL03, S07 and G318 electric and extended-range vehicles. The input shows reported funding of 6.1 billion yuan. Customers are Chinese consumers, with exports to Europe and other markets starting. Recognised brand among Chinese EV buyers.

Hesai Technology is a Shanghai-based designer and manufacturer of lidar sensors, founded in 2014, selling laser sensors for ADAS and autonomous driving to automakers like Li Auto, Lotus, Zeekr and BYD and robotaxi firms. It is one of the world's largest lidar suppliers by shipments. Listed on Nasdaq (HSAI) in 2023 and Hong Kong in 2025. Reported funding about $620 million. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

SI Flex is a South Korean supplier of flexible printed circuit boards and battery connection systems for EVs, developing and supplying components to battery and automotive makers. Based in Korea, with reported funding of about 500 billion won. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Aptera Motors is a San Diego-based start-up building the Aptera, a solar-assisted three-wheeled electric vehicle with a very aerodynamic design that claims to run on sunlight for daily driving.
